title: DOS GameMaker games with AI
author: Gooblector
selftext:
This is about 25 aI generated games, and a game editor known as Game Maker from the 90’s, now known as RSD Game Maker. 

I purchased it in 1993 after shoveling snow to raise $89 and mailed a money order (kids didn’t have credit cards back then) and it was open sourced in 2014 under MIT. I’ve used AI agents to port C and Assembly over to typescript quicker than I ever could by hand. All game maker games that I could find now work the same way in the browser. Any game you make can be exported and run on an old 286 from DOS. 

In addition, the AI has created a few games based on me, my dogs, my car, and my clown persona. 

[https://github.com/lewismoten/GameMaker-SandboxEdition](https://github.com/lewismoten/GameMaker-SandboxEdition)

We then gamified my computer desk from that period with 90’s nostalgia and added my old BBS that you could log into (emulated) and download games that the AI created using the old software. You can open retail boxes of the games and discover hint books, code wheels, and lots of “feelies”. The agents also created an in-world magazine called “Turbo Button” that reads like a game magazine of the time. There are many interactive elements on the desk, and an achievement system.

Another section is the modernized version of the software. The virtual tour guide is mostly different game characters using my voice impersonations via text to speech model and confirming clarity with whisper. You can use MCP server in the website or set it up to connect to a compatible Open API and watch it build games. 

I posted many videos of the progress on YouTube as well as video game walkthroughs made with the platforms bots that are also used to play-test levels and discover problem areas in games being created with the web-based/modern editor.

https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLdRSEx97rxwg&si=fnnSiyeSCrFjQ8pn

I also have cheap yellow displays (CYD) that can play the old DOS games, and a bare metal kernel and operating system that can also play the games on a raspberry pi zero w. 

I go back and forth between Claud and Codex on a couple of computers. For testing hardware, opus also created ghost jack that lets it control a security camera to look at different displays for testing. 

The aI has many files to keep itself in check and keep progressing on work and features. It also tracks token usage and weekly burn down charts to adjust which models it uses and how many based on remaining usage that is also displayed as a velocity report.
